design_rationale:
# Task 1 worklog — residency_occupancy_certification (Lindqvist), round 4

## 0. Draw, scope, thesis
- draw_counts.py --task 1: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5, 5]}. Assignment: mailed-form standing date 4, cycle completion date 4, closing-contact number 5, return re-dating 5.
- Claimed: residency_ext_return_contact_number (confirm_return_home_701e433e, owner=user), residency_ext_return_redating (record_return_home_baa2f4ef), residency_ext_mailed_form_standing (record_occupancy_certification_e8b1dc9f), residency_ext_cycle_completion_date (complete_certification_cycle_e152f965). Task 0 holds the four in-care policies; disjoint, union = all 8.
- Why rebuilt in round 2 (audit T1-1, T1-2, C2, C4, C5, C6): the round-1 world had two open profiles and a HECM beside an open first-lien Summit loan; the closure and phone-certification problems could not be carried by any world the base charters produce while keeping a customer's own write. The closing and phone-certification policies and tools were removed; the tree is a single-profile return home.
- Thesis: Joyce Lindqvist (81, single borrower, Standard Annual, HECM Tenure plan) was in hospital/rehab from 2026-02-23 and came home 2026-10-30. Her 2026 cycle (due 2026-07-15) passed during the monitored absence; she mailed her form signed at rehab on 2026-10-26 (received 2026-11-09). She asks that her yearly certification be done. Root: the completion date of the 2026 cycle (2026-11-09). Chain: completion waits on the form being recorded (standing 2026-10-30); the form's standing date waits on monitoring ending (the return gives the passed cycle 38 response days, due 2026-12-28); the return waits on her own confirmation recorded as a check-in (closing contact number 6).
- Base consistency (C2): the re-dating keeps the cycle in 2026 and applies only to a cycle whose due date passed during the absence; the form is recorded under certification year 2026 (calendar year of the due date the profile shows), so residency_msr_cycle_signatures reaches the Standard plan's one signature and the cycle completes; the completion tool then moves the due date to the next closing anniversary, 2027-07-15.

## 1. Problem-tree card
root completion -> mailed form (value_input, last_sig_day) -> return (value_input, monitoring_off) -> closing contact (value_input, confirm_day, owner=user).
- Sentences: "A cycle's completion date is fixed only after every accepted certification form on file for the cycle stands on the profile as a recorded certification." / "A mailed certification's standing date is fixed only after the profile shows no health-care absence under monitoring." / "The return is not recorded until the borrower's own confirmation that the borrower is back home stands on the profile as a check-in." State forms, ordering connectives, no tool/id/code token; two affirmative, one negated. One write produces each state (mailed-form tool records the form; return tool ends monitoring; return-confirmation tool is the only one writing a check-in dated after the return).
- Opening falsity: no 2026 certification entry; status absence_monitoring; latest check-in 2026-05-24 (before the return).
- Sensitivity: skip form -> no last signature (empty) instead of 2026-11-09; skip return -> standing 2026-10-26 instead of 2026-10-30; skip confirmation -> 10 response days instead of 38.
- The customer's own write: her in-person confirmation of the return (she is the only person who can attest it; given on the call).

## 2. Factor card (tier taken -> value; removal = result at that factor's baseline; solo = that factor alone against the standard rule)
Closing contact (6; standard rule 4). Assembly: highest recorded number + max(1, (DAYS(count-from, today) - grace - settling) // interval) + return-notice numbers. count_from_anchor (m: latest check-in 2026-05-24; removal 9, solo 3), closing_interval_days (p, cross hecm: three payments -> 30; removal 3, solo 10), closing_grace_days (p: return notice received 4 days after the return -> 14; removal 7, solo 3), home_settling_days (p: 8 whole months of absence at return -> 21; removal 7, solo 3), return_notice_count (p: one accepted return notice within 12 months -> 1; removal 5, solo 5). 1 + max(1, (180 - 14 - 21) // 30) + 1 = 6.
Return re-dating, scored as response days (38; standard rule -21 = due on the return date). Assembly: DAYS(today, anchor) + four allowances for a cycle that passed during the absence, else DAYS(today, due). redate_anchor_on_return (m: her confirmation 2026-11-20, 17 days after the notice's receipt (> 14) -> 0; removal 17, solo 0), documented_return_days (p: discharge summary by mail -> 14; removal 24, solo -7), long_stay_days (p: 8 whole months -> 10; removal 28, solo -11), payment_allowance_days (p, cross hecm: three payments -> 7; removal 31, solo -14), contact_allowance_days (p: exactly two check-ins -> 7; removal 31, solo -14). 0 + 14 + 10 + 7 + 7 = 38; the tool sets 2026-11-20 + 38 = 2026-12-28.
Mailed-form standing (2026-10-30; standard rule 2026-10-26). Gate structure (a factual date): the anchor date replaces the signature date only when every standing limit holds, so each factor is removal-pivotal (removal 2026-10-26 for all four) but none moves the result alone. standing_rule (m: return notice on file, signed before the return -> return date), pre_return_days (p: a check-in after the signature -> 14 vs 4), receipt_lag_days (p: return notice received before the form -> 21 vs 14), crediting_window_days (p: a certification within 18 months -> 60 vs 59 to the 2026-12-28 due date). Near-misses: the 2024/2025 mailed forms (older), the rejected portal attempt.
Completion date (2026-11-09; standard rule 2026-10-30). Gate structure as above (removal 2026-10-30 for all four, none moves it alone). completion_anchor (m: mailed, received 10 days after standing -> receipt date), return_link_days (p, multi-source: 30 vs 10), confirm_link_days (p: two check-ins -> 21 vs 11), due_window_days (p, cross hecm: three payments -> 60 days vs 49 before the due date; no payments -> 0, the standard value).
Each rule states its assembly once; every quantity the assembly names is defined, with its standard-rule value, in the standard-rule sentence. Business nexus: every ladder reads evidence about the same absence/return/form (notice promptness and documents, contacts, loan disbursements while away).

## 3. Base invariants
- Closing contact: base cadence/numbering sentence retired by the sibling overwrites (policy_scope).
- Return: monitoring ends only on an accepted return_home_notice dated before the limit (2026-10-30, 8 whole months after the 2026-02-23 start, within 12).
- Mailed form: accepted_submission bound to residency_submission_id; the once-per-signer sentence is restated in the overwrite and the rule (once per cycle under the cycle's certification_year, the calendar year of the due date the profile shows).
- Completion: the overwrite restates the due-date move to the next closing anniversary; cycle complete when the plan's required signatures are recorded under the due date's year — met by the 2026 entry.

## 4. Seed
Customer Joyce; HECM Tenure plan (closing 2018-07-15), scheduled payments 2026-06..11; profile Standard Annual, absence_monitoring since 2026-02-23, due 2026-07-15, last certified 2025-06-20; events: 2024/2025 requests and recorded certifications, check-in 1 of 2026-05-24; submissions: absence notice (admission 2026-02-23, received 2026-03-03), return notice, mailed form, rejected portal attempt (2026-05-02, outside window), 2024/2025 forms. No second profile, no payoff or Summit rows. Automatic clauses: annual request suspended during monitoring; the 180-day contact was not made; no inspection, no non-occupancy (absence under 12 months), no maturity case.

## 5. Persona
Joyce volunteers only that her rehab stay is over and that she wants her yearly certification done. On request: name, DOB, ZIP (phone). Only if asked: stay dates, that she sent her form (signed at Brightmoor on October 26), the May website attempt, living alone. Passive: gives her own confirmation when handed over, lets the agent record other items, closes when told it is complete.

## 6. Solution, verification, probes
Reads: customer, verify, profile, submissions, history, HECM, HECM transactions. Writes: Joyce confirms her return (6) -> record return (return notice, 38 response days -> due 2026-12-28) -> record mailed form (mail, 2026-10-30, year 2026) -> complete cycle (2026-11-09; due -> 2027-07-15).
Verification: scratch harness with check_compute's evaluator (gold, all-baseline, each factor at its baseline, each factor alone) reproduces every expected/baseline figure; gates green.
Edge probes (chain re-evaluated with each computed value written; columns: closing contact, response days, form standing, completion date):
    gold                                                                             [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    decoy: rejected return notice received later                                     [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    decoy: older accepted return notice (2024 stay)                                  [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    decoy: rejected mailed form received later                                       [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    decoy: accepted portal form received later (other channel)                       [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    decoy: older accepted absence notice (2023)                                      [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    decoy: second (paid-off) HECM listed first                                       [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    absent: no return notice                                                         [7, -128, '2026-10-26', '2026-10-26']
    absent: no mailed form                                                           [6, 38, '2025-06-20', '2025-06-20']
    absent: no check-in before the call; notice 8 days after start (count-from tier 3) [8, 31, '2026-10-30', '2026-10-30']
    tier: no check-in, absence notice received 60 days after start (count-from tier 2) [6, 31, '2026-10-30', '2026-10-30']
    absent: no scheduled payments (due-date window tier 3)                           [3, 31, '2026-10-30', '2026-10-30']
    tier: return notice received 2026-11-12 (anchor tier 2: confirmation 8 days later) [6, 30, '2026-10-26', '2026-11-09']
    edge: due date not passed during absence (2026-12-15)                            [6, 25, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    edge: return notice received before the return date it states                    [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    edge: form received before the signature date it states                          [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-10-30']
    edge: tie - second accepted return notice same receipt day, entered later        [7, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
    edge: tie - second accepted mailed form same receipt day, entered later          [6, 38, '2026-10-30', '2026-11-09']
Notes: with no mailed form on file the form rule would read the newest already-recorded form; the form policy is owed only while an accepted form is unrecorded, so that world never reaches it. A cycle that did not pass during the absence keeps its due date (probe above: response days to the unchanged due), so the certification year never moves away from the cycle being answered. A return notice or form received before the date it states counts as received on it (lag floored at zero, stated in rule and ladder; probes above). Return notices count toward the closing number only when received within twelve whole calendar months (an older stay's notice is a decoy). Ties on an ordering date read the record entered first (stated once in every rule). No divisor can be zero; DAYS/MONTHS never receive an empty date.

## 7. Round-2 revision log (audit 1.md T1-1..T1-4, O1; _difficulty.md C2, C4, C5, C6)
- T1-1 / C4: closure removed with its tool; one profile, no Summit, no payoff rows.
- T1-2: payoff rows removed.
- T1-3 / C2: re-dating limited to cycles that passed during the absence, same calendar year; certification year = year of the due date; cycle completes under the base measure.
- T1-4 / C5: payoff-plan, payout-plan and refinance-age conditions removed with the phone and mailed-year policies.
- C6: payoff first-match reads gone; HECM reads filtered by loan; decoys probed above.
- T1-O1: the persona no longer names a depended-on record in its opening.

## 8. Round-3 revision log (audit 1.md T1-r2-1)
- T1-r2-1: the persona's opening asked for "your file shows you are living at home again", which is the outcome of the return problem two hops below the root. The opening now says only "now that your stay in rehab is over, you want to make sure your yearly certification is done", and the closing reaction waits for "your yearly certification is complete" (no "file is up to date"). No opening or reactive line names or describes recording the return, leaving monitoring, re-dating, recording the form or any number; the only reactive line touching a prerequisite is passive (she confirms she lives in the house when the agent says Cedarline needs it and hands it over). The solvability snippets, request alignment and no_user_hint were updated to the new wording.
- N1 (obs, charter): left as is — a fix would change the rule, its compute_basis quotation and the ladder text, not one sentence; no task world reaches the overlap.

## 9. Round-4 revision log (render_source render_r1.md)
- Item 1 (assembly class): every rule carries one standard-rule sentence defining each quantity its assembly names with its default; the assembly is stated once; each factor replaces only its own quantity. Return re-dating rescored as response days (tool record_return_home_baa2f4ef takes response_days and sets the due date that many days after today): anchor + four additive allowances, each factor moving the result alone and on removal (38; standard -21). Closing-contact number: highest number + scheduled contacts + return-notice numbers (6; standard 4), the three-way numbering, first-contact offset and missed-contact cap replaced by count-from, grace, settling and return-notice factors. World re-dated: admission 2026-02-23 (notice received 2026-03-03), check-in 1 on 2026-05-24. Mailed-form standing and completion date keep their gates (factual dates: each factor removal-pivotal, none moves the date alone), with every limit defined in the standard-rule sentence and the combination stated once; the completion margin became a due-date window (receipt no more than 60 days before the due date). replaced_by texts restate the in-force base content and name their own scope.
- Item 2: the mailed-form rule no longer says the once-per-cycle recording and certification year "remain as the base rule"; it restates them (its overwrite retires that sentence). The completion rule no longer says the due-date move "remains as the base rule"; its overwrite restates the move to the next closing anniversary.
- Item 3: the closing grace (formerly closing allowance), the re-dating anchor and the form/receipt lags state a notice or form received before the date it states (counted as received on it) in rule, ladder and compute; the minimum-absence and first-offset ladders are gone.
- Item 4: the return re-dating replaced_by no longer says "within response_grace_days of the return or of its confirmation"; it now reads "is re-dated under this policy, while a cycle whose due date did not pass during the absence keeps the due date the profile shows".

## 10. Round-5 revision log (policy_task revision_4: R4-1..R4-5)
- R4-1 (c): the return re-dating anchor no longer tests the confirmation's existence (the prerequisite guarantees it): confirmation date where it came more than 14 days after the notice's receipt / notice receipt where the notice came more than 7 days after the return / return date. Same class: the contact allowance tiers are three or more check-ins 10 / exactly two 7 / only the confirmation 0.
- R4-1 (e): closing-contact count-from is the latest check-in / the absence notice's receipt where no check-in is recorded and it came more than 45 days after the start / the start.
- R4-1 (f): the mailed-form anchor tiers no longer restate the monitoring prerequisite; the prerequisite edge now bears on due_on_file (the crediting window is measured to the due date fixed on the return).
- R4-3: completion due-date window fall-through is zero days (no scheduled payments or no HECM loan), equal to its baseline; 1-2 payments give 45.
- The completion gate states that an anchor before the return date or a contact before the anchor counts as zero days (MX(0, ...) in the compute). Ties on every "latest" pick are covered by the stated tie sentence and probed (same-day return notices and mailed forms). Scored values unchanged (6, 38, 2026-10-30, 2026-11-09); skip-confirmation figure now 10.

## 11. Round-6 revision log (render_source render_r2.md)
- Rule-vs-compute miss (return re-dating, anchor tier 1): the compute now reads the return notice's receipt exactly as the rule defines it — a notice received before the return date it states counts as received on that date (return_received = MX(return date, receipt)). Probes on this world: notice received 2026-10-20 (counts as 2026-10-30), confirmation 2026-11-20 -> anchor stays the confirmation, 38; notice received 2026-10-01 with the confirmation handled on 2026-11-09 -> counted receipt 2026-10-30, confirmation 10 days later (<= 14), anchor = return date, 28 (the unclamped read would have given 38). Gold unchanged (38).
- Sweep of every "counting as received on it" read: facility letter receipt now clamped the same way (MX(contact date, receipt)); report lag, mailed-form receipt, completion form receipt and the closing-grace lag were already clamped; the absence-start gate states "counts as zero days" and clamps. No scored value moved.
- Minors: the return contact allowance now states its zero-check-in branch ("or none is") in rule and ladder; the call-in prerequisite effect text says the numbering basis is one without the facility contact (and names the notice-receipt count-from case); the completion overwrite's replaced_by ends with a full stop, so the rule no longer reads "; A cycle's".
user_scenario:
You are Joyce Marie Lindqvist, eighty-one, calling Cedarline from the kitchen of your house at 9140 Ballantyne Commons Drive in Charlotte, which carries your reverse mortgage. You are brisk and organised, with a notepad in front of you, glad to be home and a little impatient with paperwork, though never rude.

You open by saying that, now that your stay in rehab is over, you want to make sure your yearly certification is done. That is what you want taken care of today.

When the agent asks who is calling, you give your full name, Joyce Marie Lindqvist. To confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1945-09-14, and the ZIP code of the house, 28277; if they want your phone number, it is 4155532209. You do not have account or reference numbers memorised and tell the agent to look you up by name.

Only if the agent asks about your stay do you explain that you were admitted to Novant Health Presbyterian on February 23 after a fall, went on to Brightmoor Rehabilitation, and came home on October 30, and that you mailed your discharge summary in right away. If they ask whether you sent in your yearly certification form, you say yes: you filled in and signed it at Brightmoor on October 26 because you knew you were going home that week, and mailed it once you were settled; if they ask about the website, you say you tried to certify online back in May and it was not accepted. If they ask whether anyone else lives with you, you say you live alone. You cannot tell them dates from Cedarline's own records and say they will have to look.

If the agent tells you that Cedarline needs you yourself to confirm that you are back living in the house, you say of course, and when they hand that confirmation over to you, you give it using exactly the reference and the number they tell you, asking them to repeat anything you did not catch, and you read back the confirmation you receive. If they say there are other things on their side to record first, you tell them to go ahead and you wait. Once the agent tells you your yearly certification is complete, you thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: residency_events carries a residency_certification_recorded entry under the open cycle's certification year for each accepted occupancy certification form on file for the cycle (residency_submission_id).
edges.policy_source: A cycle's completion date is fixed only after every accepted certification form on file for the cycle stands on the profile as a recorded certification.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Joyce's accepted mailed certification form (signed 2026-10-26, received 2026-11-09) has no certification entry; nothing is recorded under the 2026 cycle.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The mailed-form write records the certification under certification year 2026 standing on 2026-10-30, which becomes the cycle's last signature; the completion date then reads its form's receipt 2026-11-09.

edges.condition: residency_profiles.status is not absence_monitoring and residency_profiles.absence_start_date is empty, the return having been recorded with the due date it fixes.
edges.policy_source: A mailed certification's standing date is fixed only after the profile shows no health-care absence under monitoring.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The profile still shows the health-care absence under monitoring although the return notice is accepted.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The return write sets status current, clears the absence start and gives the 2026 cycle 38 response days (due 2026-12-28); the crediting window is then measured to that due date and the form signed before the return stands on the return date 2026-10-30 instead of 2026-10-26.

edges.condition: residency_events carries a residency_absence_checkin entry for the profile dated on or after the return date on the accepted return-home notice (the borrower's own closing contact).
edges.policy_source: The return is not recorded until the borrower's own confirmation that the borrower is back home stands on the profile as a check-in.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only check-in on the profile is check-in 1 of 2026-05-24; nothing dated on or after the 2026-10-30 return records Joyce's own confirmation.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Joyce's own confirmation is recorded as check-in 6 dated 2026-11-20, 17 days after the notice's receipt; the re-dating anchor becomes 2026-11-20 instead of the return date 2026-10-30 (the notice came 4 days after the return) and the contact allowance counts two check-ins.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is one chain (cycle completion -> mailed form -> return -> Joyce's confirmation), so the only topological order is confirmation, return, mailed form, completion; each value is computed on the world the earlier writes leave.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the mailed-form write leaves no signature under the 2026 cycle: the completion date has no last signature (empty) instead of 2026-11-09, and the terminal history lacks the certification entry.

Skipping the return write leaves the profile under monitoring with the passed due date 2026-07-15, which precedes the anchor date 2026-10-30, so the form stands on its stated 2026-10-26 instead of 2026-10-30; the terminal profile keeps status absence_monitoring and due 2026-07-15.

Skipping Joyce's confirmation leaves no check-in on or after the return: the re-dating anchor falls to the return date 2026-10-30 (-21 days; the notice came 4 days after the return) and the contact allowance to zero, so the response days recompute to 10 instead of 38, and the closing contact is missing from the history.
